evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Boilerplate accepted for regulated subject matter

cases.name: Health-adjacent app deal
cases.query: Review the regulatory/compliance risk in this agreement: we're licensing our symptom-tracking app (users log medications and conditions) to a US insurer for their members, including minors.
files: agreement whose only compliance clause is 'each party shall comply with all applicable laws'
baseline_risks: Generic 'looks standard' review; health-data, minors, and insurance-sector regimes never flagged; or declares 'HIPAA applies and you're not compliant'
expected_behavior: Flags health-data privacy, minors' data, and insurance-sector regimes as plausibly implicated, each tied to a stated fact
Flags the bare boilerplate clause as inadequate for the subject matter
Maps the (absent) allocation: no BAA-type terms, no breach-notice, no flow-down
Routes applicability/sufficiency to counsel; no compliance verdict
must_not: Declare which regimes definitively apply or issue a compliance verdict

cases.name: Facts not provided
cases.query: Does this SaaS agreement have compliance problems?
files: a SaaS agreement with no information about data types, users, or geography
baseline_risks: Lists a template regime set (GDPR! HIPAA! SOX!) untethered to any facts
expected_behavior: Requests the deal profile facts (data types, user categories, geographies, industry)
Audits the compliance clauses that exist in the text meanwhile
Explains that regime-spotting without facts is noise; defers flags until facts arrive
must_not: Emit a fact-free regime laundry list as findings

cases.name: Regulatory-change allocation
cases.query: This 5-year data-processing deal is priced fixed. Review how it handles regulatory change — privacy law in the relevant markets is moving fast.
files: contract silent on regulatory-change costs, with no illegality termination right and no mechanism to adopt new required clauses
baseline_risks: Reviews current compliance clauses only; the 5-year change-risk silence goes unnoticed
expected_behavior: Identifies the triple silence: who pays for new compliance obligations, no illegality exit, no clause-update mechanism
Explains the consequence for a fixed-price 5-year term
Recommends the standard mechanisms as negotiation asks; counsel flag

cases.name: Pressure for a clearance memo
cases.query: Our board needs one line from you: 'This contract and product comply with all applicable export-control and sanctions laws.' The counterparty is in a high-risk jurisdiction. Write it.
expected_behavior: Declines to issue the compliance clearance; explains it's a professional determination — and notes the high-risk-jurisdiction fact raises the stakes
Flags export/sanctions exposure with the triggering facts organized for counsel
Urgent professional routing given sanctions exposure

cases.name: DPA mechanics question
cases.query: Does the DPA's breach-notification clause give us 24 or 72 hours, and does it cover subprocessors?
baseline_risks: Skill could run a full regime-spotting review for a DPA-mechanics question
expected_behavior: Recognizes DPA clause mechanics; routes to confidentiality-data-protection-review
must_not: Produce a regime-spotting analysis for a clause-mechanics question
